newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE trades record volume in first half of 1997.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE trades record volume in first half of 1997.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Wednesday it had traded a record 100.99 million futures and options contracts in the first half of 1997, the first time the exchange has traded over 100 million contracts in a half-year.
Volume was up 22 percent on the first half of 1996 when LIFFE traded 82.91 million contracts.
LIFFE also had its busiest June ever, trading a record 17.04 million futures and options contracts, up 35 percent on June 1996.

"In this, its fifteenth anniversary year, LIFFE has set a new half-year volume record and was the second-largest futures and options exchange in the world for the half year," said Jack Wigglesworth, LIFFE's chairman.
In the past month, three-month Eurolira futures set a new monthly record of over 1.401 million contracts compared with the previous monthly record of over 1.237 million set in April 1997.
Three month Euroswiss futures also set a new monthly record of 458,919, beating the previous record of 418,953 set in May 1997.
LIFFE's total for the year-to-date volume does not include German Bund futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) as a result of the LIFFE/CBOT link.
LIFFE said since the launch of the link on May 9, a total of 142,122 Bund futures and a total of 11,529 Bund options had been traded.
